facts.text: In the United States, OSHA writes and enforces construction safety rules, MSHA writes and enforces mine safety rules, and NIOSH conducts research that informs both agencies.
facts.quote: OSHA writes and enforces construction safety rules, MSHA does the same for mines, and NIOSH is the research institute whose studies and tests inform both

entities.name: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health

facts.text: OSHA rules 29 CFR 1926.601(b)(4) and 1926.602(a)(9)(ii) require a reverse signal alarm audible above surrounding noise, or an observer, when a machine's rear view is obstructed.
facts.quote: Rules 29 CFR 1926.601(b)(4) and 1926.602(a)(9)(ii) require a reverse signal alarm audible above surrounding noise, or an observer, when a machine's rear view is obstructed.

facts.text: OSHA interpretation letters accept a camera as removing the obstructed-view trigger for reverse-warning requirements if the camera truly provides a clear view.
facts.quote: a camera can remove the "obstructed view" trigger if it truly provides a clear view

facts.text: OSHA interpretation letters accept radar warning as satisfying the reverse-warning rule where radar warns in time.
facts.quote: radar warning can satisfy the rule where it warns in time.

facts.text: OSHA's reverse-warning rules specify no numeric range and impose no automatic-brake mandate.
facts.quote: There is no numeric range and no automatic-brake mandate [Chapter 3].

facts.text: MSHA regulates mines under title 30 of the Code of Federal Regulations.
facts.quote: The Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) regulates mines under title 30 of the Code of Federal Regulations.

facts.text: For surface coal mines, 30 CFR 77.410 requires loaders, trucks, graders and similar equipment to have a reverse alarm or discriminating detection using infrared, ultrasonic, radar or another effective device, with a sensing area large enough for an endangered person to escape.
facts.quote: 30 CFR 77.410 (surface coal) requires, for loaders, trucks, graders and similar equipment, a reverse alarm or discriminating detection "using infrared, ultrasonic, radar, or another effective device", with a sensing area large enough for an endangered person to escape

facts.text: Lidar is not named in 30 CFR 77.410 and should not be called "approved" under that rule.
facts.quote: lidar is not named, so it should not be called "approved" [Chapter 3].

facts.text: For metal and non-metal mines, 30 CFR 56.14132 and 57.14132 require a reverse-activated alarm, alternatives or an observer.
facts.quote: 30 CFR 56.14132 and 57.14132 (metal and non-metal mines) require a reverse-activated alarm, alternatives or an observer.

facts.text: 30 CFR 75.1732 (2015) requires proximity detection on underground continuous mining machines that warns and then stops the machine before contacting a miner.
facts.quote: 30 CFR 75.1732 (2015) requires proximity detection on continuous mining machines underground: warn, then stop before contacting a miner

facts.text: 30 CFR 75.1732 specifies no numeric distance after proposed values of 3 ft and 5 ft were dropped.
facts.quote: with no numeric distance after the proposed 3 ft and 5 ft values were dropped [Chapter 3].

facts.text: The Safety Program for Surface Mobile Equipment rule requires compliance from 17 July 2024 with mine-specific written programs evaluating currently available and newly emerging feasible technologies.
facts.quote: The Safety Program for Surface Mobile Equipment rule (compliance from 17 July 2024) requires mine-specific written programs that evaluate "currently available and newly emerging feasible technologies"

entities.name: Safety Program for Surface Mobile Equipment rule

facts.text: The Safety Program for Surface Mobile Equipment rule does not mandate collision avoidance.
facts.quote: it does not mandate collision avoidance

entities.name: Safety Program for Surface Mobile Equipment rule

facts.text: By April 2026, 863 citations had been issued under the Safety Program for Surface Mobile Equipment rule.
facts.quote: 863 citations had been issued by April 2026 [Chapter 3].

entities.name: Safety Program for Surface Mobile Equipment rule

facts.text: The booklet did not find a United States federal rule requiring a machine to command its own brakes after an ignored warning.
facts.quote: A federal rule requiring a machine to command its own brakes after an ignored warning was not found [Chapter 3].

facts.text: NIOSH's 2000 haul-truck tests defined reliable detection as an alarm within 200 ms.
facts.quote: its 2000 haul-truck tests defining "reliable" detection as an alarm within 200 ms

entities.name: National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health
